script_wording: In nineteen seventy-two, a French lab tested uranium from a mine in Gabon. Some of its fuel was missing.
primary_source: IAEA (2018) Meet Oklo https://www.iaea.org/node/51357 ; Ragheb lecture notes https://www.mragheb.com/NPRE%20402%20ME%20405%20Nuclear%20Power%20Engineering/Natural%20%20Nuclear%20Reactors
evidence_category: IAEA page para on Francis Perrin; Ragheb sec 6.1 and 6.3 (Pierrelatte enrichment plant May 1972)
intended_visual: Lab = French fuel processing / enrichment plant (Pierrelatte); avoid naming a single discoverer as sole credit
confidence: 1970s lab: low poly scientist at instrument; sample vial labelled Gabon

script_wording: Natural uranium almost everywhere holds the same tiny share of uranium two thirty five: zero point seven two percent. This ore had less.
location: Expected 0.7202 %, measured 0.7171 %; some samples down to 0.44 %
caveat: "Almost everywhere" (Oklo is the exception); exact figure 0.720 %

script_wording: Like fuel that had already been burned in a reactor. But this was a rock. Nobody had built anything.
location: Fission product footprint confirmed natural fission
caveat: Analogy: depletion pattern resembles spent fuel; investigators also had to rule out contamination
intended_visual: Comparison: reactor fuel rod vs ore rock

script_wording: About two billion years ago, uranium was richer: roughly three percent uranium two thirty five, close to what our power reactors use.
primary_source: Shlyakhter (1982) arXiv physics/0307023 ; decay calculation in this ledger
location: Shlyakhter: "about 3 percent"; computed 2.9 % at 1.7 Gyr, 3.7 % at 2.0 Gyr
caveat: Age quoted 1.7 to 2.0 Gyr in sources; say about two billion; commercial fuel typically 3 to 5 %
intended_visual: Uranium gauge rewinds from 0.72 % to about 3 %

script_wording: Groundwater soaked the ore. Water slows neutrons down, so they split uranium more easily. A chain reaction started on its own.
primary_source: Ragheb sec 6.1 and 6.4; Meshik et al. 2004 PRL 93 182302
caveat: Schematic; atoms not to scale; neutron speeds stylised
intended_visual: Cutaway: water in pores; neutron slows in water then splits nucleus; cascade

script_wording: Then its heat boiled the water away. Without it, the reaction stopped. The rock cooled, water seeped back in, and it switched on again.
primary_source: Meshik et al. 2004 PRL 93 182302 (via Physics Today 2004 summary https://physicstoday.aip.org/news/the-cycle-of-the-natural-nuclear-reactor)
location: Xenon isotopes in aluminium phosphate grains reveal on/off cycle
caveat: Cycle inferred for one reactor zone; mechanism (boil off / return) is the authors' interpretation
intended_visual: Water gauge falls; reactor chip OFF; water returns; ON again

script_wording: About half an hour on, a few hours off, for over a hundred thousand years.
primary_source: Meshik et al. 2004; Physics Today 2004; Ragheb sec 6.8
location: 30 min on, at least 2.5 h off; lifetime about 150,000 years (Ragheb also gives several hundred thousand)
caveat: Durations are estimates; say over a hundred thousand years
intended_visual: Clock / cycle counter loops; time compression labelled

script_wording: It can't happen today. Uranium two thirty five decays faster than the rest, and natural ore no longer has enough.
location: "no natural reactor could operate today with uranium containing only 0.72 percent"
caveat: Holds for natural ore with ordinary water; heavy water or graphite reactors can run on natural uranium, so phrase as natural ore
intended_visual: Gauge falls from 3 % to 0.72 % across time; dim ore

script_wording: But the rock kept the receipts. Its leftovers show that one of the fundamental constants of physics has changed by less than one part in ten million in two billion years.
primary_source: Damour & Dyson 1996 Nucl. Phys. B arXiv hep-ph/9606486
location: 95 % C.L. bound on Δα/α about -0.9e-7 to 1.2e-7 over about 2 Gyr
caveat: Applies to the fine structure constant under the paper's assumptions; later analyses refine the bound
intended_visual: Samarium readout; constant symbol α with tight band

script_wording: A nuclear reactor nobody built... and it's still teaching us.
intended_visual: Return to 1970s lab sample; camera pulls out
